correctness.rationale: Unwrapping in the shortest angular class gives squared intrinsic and ambient distances r²(θ²+x²) and r²(4 sin²(θ/2)+x²). The independent angular and normalized axial differences have densities 1/π and 2(1-v), respectively. This yields the exact threshold formula; for any two positive heights its integrand drops strictly on a positive-length interval just above θ_t. The ratio extends continuously at coincidence with value 1 by its axial-independent bound θ/(2 sin(θ/2)); continuity and positive-measure neighborhoods establish the essential range, with the stated maximizing distinct pairs. At the maximum the loss in (δ,x²) is δ/2+βx² plus a quadratic remainder. Positivity localizes δ=O(ε), x=O(√ε). After scaling the remainder lies in a level shell of width O(ε) in scaled variables; the fixed-height density correction is O_h(√ε), giving precisely the stated ε^(3/2) coefficient and O_h(ε²) remainder. Squaring the axial coordinate in the uniform parabolic limit gives the claimed Dirichlet density. For bounded λ, sandwiching the angular admissible length at fixed v between 2[ε(1−βλ²v²)±O_Λ(ε²)]_+ gives a uniform error including at clipping. Integration yields both branches, with third derivative jump 8/π in L=λ√β. Independent axial-first integration at fixed h and across the clipping point corroborates the coefficients.
residual_risks: Numerical replay is corroboration only; claims about uniformity at unbounded λ and other endpoint measures were not tested or inferred.

value.rationale: The coupled metric distortion is a natural observable not captured by either metric alone. The exact probability law identifies height-to-radius from one fixed threshold; the explicit crossover quantifies when fixed-height rare-event behavior ceases to describe a thin cylinder and detects a specific nonanalytic transition from the axial cutoff. Together with the conditional limit, this goes beyond a routine distance computation.
residual_risks: Value is for this normalized sidewall model, not a claim about arbitrary developable surfaces or other collapse regimes.
